To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The incidence of HCC in the United States is rising; 2) HCC has a poor prognosis; 3) HCC is the most common cancer of the liver; 4) HCC is a leading cause of death in the United States; 5) There are many risk factors for HCC, including alcohol abuse, hepatitis B virus (HBV), and hepatitis C virus (HCV); 6) HCC can be diagnosed by imaging, biopsy,
HBV infection can induce hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), which has been associated with the expression of apoptotic genes.

HBV infection is associated with the down-regulation of the expression of Bcl-2, Bcl-XL, survivin, and XIAP proteins, and up-regulation of caspase-3, caspase-8, and caspase-9 proteins, in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of Bcl-2 family proteins and caspase-3 proteins in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
the expression of apoptosis-related proteins in HBV-infected hepatocarcinomas and non-HBV-related hepatocarcinoma.
the role that HBV plays in the development of HCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HBV-infected HCC has a worse prognosis and that HBV-infec- tion has a significant impact on the prognosis of HCC patients.
